note: The boundary between Villacana and the paseo/Barraka beach along the big-pool lawn: a white wall from the end of the sandstone wall, down beside the paseo ramp, to an arched gateway at the lawn's south-west corner, a short white wall, then white railings along the lawn to its east end. Turned-frame metres (sea downward); every line is 1.75 m inland of the paseo's centre line, just off the 3 m paving. Heights are metres above the paseo.
trust: Dave, 2026-10-21: a fence and a coastal gate run in front of the slope, separating Villacana from Barraka beach. IMG_2226 (from the beach, looking north-west) shows, west to east, a white wall with a tiled panel, a white arched gateway at paseo level, a short white wall and white railings along the lawn up to Barraka's raised deck; IMG_2227 shows the white tiled wall where the sandstone wall ends; apple-maps/11 shows the gateway at the bottom of the lane with the zebra crossing in front. Positions follow the paseo line (plan about 1-2 m); the gateway sits where the lane meets it. Heights (wall 1.5 m, railings 1.1 m, arch 2.4 m), the 1.4 m opening and the bar spacing are read by eye, not measured. The gateway opening stays clear. IMG_2602 and IMG_2759 show a dark iron leaf, drawn swung open. Dave, 2026-10-27: the beach entrance is not at the end of the slope but to its left looking at the beach. Moved 7.5 m north-east along the same line to the dark gateway the aerial shows at the lawn's south-west corner (about scene -6, 131.5), which also agrees within compass error with the arch's bearing in IMG_2226; the wall is split into 1.5 m runs so it steps down the ramp. Ground there from the laser survey (main_pool.json seafront profile). 2026-11-04 (barraka-frontage-paseo-furniture): close photos from the paseo (IMG_2604, 2609, 2610, 2630, 2631; also IMG_2484 for the mesh-panel stretch near the gateway) show the lawn railing as dark green vertical bars with square posts on a low sandstone-block plinth, not the white railings read from the beach at 50 m in IMG_2226 (the pale line there is probably the white pool-side building). Only the finish changed (bars, posts and rail now dark green, plinth sandstone); heights (railing 1.1 m, plinth 0.3 m; the photos suggest the plinth is nearer 0.5 m) and collision are unchanged. 13 Nov: the railing had been a straight chord from the gateway to Barraka's corner, across the grass, so the wall enclosed the pool and cut the private lawn in two. IMG_2760 looks across that lawn to a fence at the far edge, with Barraka beyond; IMG_2604, IMG_2611, IMG_2630 and IMG_2610 show the same green fence following the path. The line now follows the path's lawn edge, traced from the aerial, and the pool stays open to the lawn.

rampWall.note: Dave, 2026-11-13: the slope down has no opening; the only way out is the gate. The ramp wall now starts where the corner wall ends, closing the 2.3 m gap the foot of Calle Guillermo ran out through. IMG_2600 and IMG_2601 show the inner tiled path from the lane's foot ending at a hedge and a mesh fence, not at an opening.

gate.note: Shape from IMG_2602 (inside), IMG_2766 (paseo) and IMG_2485 (close): two square white piers, a rectangular opening about 1.25 m wide and 2.1 m high with a black iron leaf with ring motifs, a flat moulded lintel and above it a shallow segmental hood with a projecting cornice, about 2.85 m at its crown; the COMUNIDAD VILLACANA sign is on the paseo face of the wall beside it. Sizes by eye against the 2 m leaf (2026-11-13); it replaces a round-arched slab.
